result.title: GRAFT: Graph-Regularized Prototype Fields for Realistic Test-Time Adaptation of VLMs
result.summary: Unlabeled test data can improve the zero-shot classifier of a vision-language model, yet transductive and test-time adaptation methods often fall below the zero-shot baseline when only a few vocabulary classes are present in a batch or when streams are correlated. We trace this failure to a shared design: every class owns independent parameters estimated from its own samples, so absent or rare classes are left at biased text anchors or fitted to foreign samples. We propose Graph-Regularized Anchor-displacement Field Transduction (GRAFT), which models the adapted prototypes as text anchors plus a displacement field that is partially pooled over a semantic class graph through a Gaussian Markov random field prior, together with an explicit class-presence model. Inference is closed-form and gradient-free on cached features. Anchor-only shrinkage and a single global shift are the two extreme settings of the prior; absent classes are provably harmonic extensions of the present ones, and the pooling strength can be chosen by empirical Bayes. Under the realistic batch and online protocols on eleven benchmarks and four ImageNet shifts, GRAFT improves over the zero-shot model in every setting and over anchor-based transduction where few classes are present.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GRAFT，把测试时适应后的类原型表示为文本锚点加位移场，用语义类图上的高斯马尔可夫随机场先验做部分池化并引入显式类存在模型，在缓存特征上以闭式、无梯度方式推理，改善少类批次与相关流下的 VLM 适应。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及视觉推理中的 latent 状态，但其「锚点＋位移场」的部分池化与类存在建模，可能为 latent 表示的正则化、缺失证据下的状态补全与存在性判别提供方法线索，可供核查。
